claim: CyberGym evaluates AI agents on 1,507 real-world vulnerability-reproduction instances collected from OSS-Fuzz across 188 large-scale software projects, requiring agents to generate a PoC that triggers on the pre-patch but not post-patch codebase version.
stance_target: benchmark design for autonomous vulnerability discovery/reproduction
quoted_support: We collect 1,507 benchmark instances by systematically gathering real-world vulnerabilities discovered and patched across 188 widely distributed and large-scale software projects.

claim: In open-ended vulnerability discovery across 431 OSS-Fuzz projects (1,748 executables), OpenHands with GPT-5 triggered 56 crashes yielding 22 confirmed zero-day vulnerabilities, versus GPT-4.1's 16 crashes yielding 7 confirmed zero-days.
stance_target: measured capability ceiling of frontier models for autonomous vulnerability discovery at scale
scope_conditions: CyberGym open-ended discovery evaluation, GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 via OpenHands, 2026
quoted_support: GPT-4.1 triggered 16 crashes, leading to 7 confirmed zero-days. GPT-5 triggered 56 crashes, yielding 22 confirmed zero-days (4 overlapping).

claim: Across the full CyberGym evaluation, AI-agent-generated PoCs surfaced 34 zero-day vulnerabilities and 18 historically incomplete patches, with discovered zero-days persisting an average of 969 days before discovery.
stance_target: real-world security impact of agentic vulnerability discovery, beyond benchmark scores
quoted_support: The agents not only reproduced known vulnerabilities, they uncovered incomplete patches and previously unknown zero-day bugs. 34 zero-day vulnerabilities, 18 incomplete patches ... 969 avg. days undiscovered

claim: Extended reasoning ('thinking mode') increases GPT-5's vulnerability-reproduction success rate from 7.7% (minimal reasoning) to 22.0% (high reasoning) on a 300-task CyberGym subset, surpassing Claude-Sonnet-4.
stance_target: effect of reasoning-depth/compute allocation on agentic security task success
scope_conditions: CyberGym, 300-task subset, models: Qwen3-235B-A22B, GPT-5, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Claude-Sonnet-4
quoted_support: While thinking mode yields modest gains for most models, it increases GPT-5's success rate from 7.7% (minimal reasoning) to 22.0% (high reasoning), surpassing Claude-Sonnet-4.

claim: Only 3.5% of CyberGym Level-0 instances (text description only, no stack trace or patch) can be reproduced, showing richer input context is critical for agentic vulnerability reproduction.
stance_target: input-context richness as a dominant factor in agentic security-task success, relevant to context-isolation design for security-sweep agents
quoted_support: Richer input — such as the stack trace in level 2 and ground-truth patch in level 3 — greatly enhances the vulnerability reproduction success rate compared to level 1 (our primary task). For level 0, only 3.5% of instances can be reproduced without access to the text description of the target vulnerability.

claim: With OpenHands/Claude-4-Sonnet and a 100-step execution cap, nearly half of all CyberGym runs terminate at steps 80-100 without success, while successful runs concentrate in steps 20-80 (peaking 20-50), suggesting a 100-step budget is a reasonable solve/resource tradeoff for autonomous security agents.
stance_target: appropriate step/compute budget allocation for autonomous security-agent tasks
quoted_support: successful outcomes concentrate between steps 20–80, peaking at 20–50. However, nearly half of runs terminate at 80–100 steps without success. ... The 100-step limit offers an effective balance between solving capacity and resource use.
